walk.environment:
Build: the read-only worktree /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/tree at 0deff9c4. Every server ran from it through /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P/launch.py, which drops HTTP(S)_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY, OO_DB_PASSPHRASE and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT, sets PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, chdirs to the tree and execs `.venv/bin/python -c "from src.api.main import main; main()"`. All runs used port 8921, one server at a time: folder A, then folder A again after the restart, then folder B. Every server was stopped by PID (22371 and 23350 for A, 23548 for B); the first A exited through the app's own power icon. No data folder was copied from the first walk; both were built fresh.

Folder A (/tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P/dataA): fresh, started with OO_AUTOSEED=0 and made ENCRYPTED through the real first-launch screens (language, legal, the 'Where should your corpus live?' step, passphrase walk-pass-2026). /api/system/lock-state read 'fresh', then 'unlocked-encrypted'. After the power-icon quit and relaunch it read 'locked' and was unlocked through #pw / #btn-unlock.

Folder B (/tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P/dataB): seeded at 08:07 UTC on 2026-09-27 (machine timezone UTC, so after 03:00 and the expected 'changes today' is 4). First scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py (453 articles), then docs/audit/living-sources-clickthrough-2026-09-25/seed.py, copied to /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P/seed_living.py and run with PYTHONPATH=tree. Both seeds ran with OO_DB_PASSPHRASE=walk-pass-2026 and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT unset. The first 16 bytes of open_omniscience.db and wiki.db are ciphertext, not 'SQLite format 3'. B was booted with neither variable set. lock-state read 'locked', and the unlock went through #pw.

Every log reads 'Booted in airplane mode (offline)', /api/system/network answered online:false at every check, and 'Go online' was never pressed. Every consent popup was opened, read, screenshotted and closed with 'Stay offline'.

Harness setup, disclosed: between the three language passes of P11, W was put back to 'running' with a loopback PUT /api/scheduler/config {wiki_lane_state:'running'} followed by a reload. Offline there is no UI path back from stopped to running without consent. With the kill switch engaged the server does not start the lane (src/api/scheduler.py _apply_wiki_lane_state), and network stayed online:false.

Browser: Playwright Chromium /opt/pw-browsers/chromium, headless, args --disable-background-networking --disable-component-update --no-proxy-server --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage, launched with the proxy variables unset. A request listener logged 0 off-host requests. The main pass ran at 1440x950 in en, then live switches to ar, zh and fr through #lang-switch. 375x800 passes ran in en, and also in fr and ar.

walk.summary:
Row P re-walked on the fixed build 0deff9c4. Both folders were encrypted and locked at boot, the walk stayed in airplane mode throughout, and 'Go online' was never pressed. All ten confirmed row-P defects are fixed:
- Hover bubbles now show inside modal dialogs: the consent popup's per-lane hosts and transport line, and the export row's reason.
- The W bubble no longer goes stale after a click; neither does the gauge's.
- The reader's external-link confirm is translated.
- The first-launch data-location step answers 200.
- The Shift+click stop is named in the W hover.
- The popup lists Wikipedia as it will be once started, and the toasts confirm the state.
- The Home strip's source-split labels are translated.
- The Living sources export reason is translated, and byte units are localized.
- Settings → Wikipedia no longer scrolls sideways at 375 px.
- ORES starts unticked.

The overlapping defects from other rows that I could check are also fixed: H1, H2, H3, H7, H8, I15/U1, O1, S4, T4, T7, U5 and U8.

Steps P1-P4 and P6-P10 pass in en, and in ar, zh and fr where walked. P5 is not measurable after consent. Its offline parts pass: consent gate, restart into airplane mode, default-on boot held offline.

P11 fails on one point. In Arabic, the Wikipedia wizard's host line breaks '*.wikipedia.org': the '*.' is drawn at the far end of the line. This is the H3 class of defect on a surface H3's fix did not cover (new, P3).

The 375 px pass is clean in en. In French, the Home strip scrolls sideways by 28 px and clips its labels (new, P3).

Two more new P3s:
- On an idle, offline app, the Home strip says 'as of 08:20 AM (server busy)' even though the counts are current.
- The search palette shows the same Wikipedia page twice with identical labels that open different things.

No page errors, no HTTP errors >= 400 from the app, no undefined/NaN/null/[object Object] text, and no off-host browser requests. The only console errors were the expected ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED after the power-icon shutdown. The one 404 in the logs was my own curl to /api/stats and is excluded.

items.evidence: I used my own fresh folder, /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P-recheck/dataB. I seeded it with scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py plus a copy of the living-sources seed, with OO_DB_PASSPHRASE=walk-pass-2026 and OO_DB_PLAINTEXT unset. The first 16 bytes of both .db files are ciphertext. I booted it on port 8971 with neither variable set. lock-state read 'locked' and I unlocked through #pw / #btn-unlock. The log says 'Booted in airplane mode (offline)'. At 1440x950 I switched #lang-switch live to en, ar, zh and fr, and each time opened Settings → Wikipedia → #wiki-wizard-open. In en, zh and fr, #wiki-wizard-hosts reads '*.wikipedia.org · stream.wikimedia.org · wikimedia.org · ores.wikimedia.org · dumps.wikimedia.org' left to right: '*' at x=399, then 'w' at x=413. In ar the element has direction rtl and no isolate characters. The '*' glyph is drawn at x=1034 and the '.' after it at x=1027, which is the far right end of line 1, while the 'w' of 'wikipedia' starts the line at x=487. On screen that is 'wikipedia.org · stream.wikimedia.org · wikimedia.org · ores.wikimedia.org ·.*', with 'dumps.wikimedia.org' on line 2. The same happens at 375 px. As a control, the consent popup's Wikipedia-lane bubble in ar is fixed: each host is wrapped in U+2066/U+2069 and '*' (x=1105) sits before 'w' (x=1115). Every consent popup was cancelled and network stayed online:false. There were no page errors, console errors, HTTP >= 400 or off-host requests. Shots: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P-recheck/shots/Prc-wizard-ar.png, Prc-zoom-wizard-hosts-ar.png, Prc-zoom-wizard-hosts-en.png, Prc-N375-zoom-wizard-hosts-ar.png, Prc-consent-wiki-hover-ar.png. items.root_cause: src/static/app-sources.js:1388 (_wizPaintHosts) sets el.textContent = hosts.join(' · ') with no LTR isolation. It sits inside the RTL dialog, so the bidi algorithm moves the neutral leading '*.' of '*.wikipedia.org' to the visual end of the line. The H3 fix wrapped hosts in isolates only in src/static/app-core.js:1329 (_laneHostTitle, the consent bubble), not in this second place that renders the same host table.
items.suggested_fix: Give the host line dir="ltr" in index.html:3469, since host names are always LTR tokens. Or wrap each host as the consent bubble does: hosts.map(h => '⁦' + h + '⁩').join(' · '). A small node or pytest check should then pin both call sites.

items.ref: new:Home strip says 'as of 08:20 AM (server busy)' on an idle, offline app whose counts are current
items.evidence: My own instance, en, 1440x950, idle and offline: scheduler running:false and /api/system/network online:false throughout. At 10:13:00 /api/database/stats returned as_of 10:11:59, cache_age_s 60, and the strip showed no note. By 10:13:49 cache_age_s was 109, and after a live switch to fr and back and after a reload the strip read 'as of 10:11 AM (server busy)'. fr reads 'à 10:11 (serveur occupé)' and ar reads 'حتى 10:11 ص (الخادم مشغول)'. Four curl samples 20 s apart (10:14:15 to 10:15:15) returned the same built_at 10:11:59, with age going 135 → 155 → 175 → 195 against cache_ttl_s 30. By served_cache.cached, an entry past its TTL keeps its built_at only when the write-gate probe is unchanged, so the server itself had verified that nothing was written and the counts were exact. The server log has no 'served-cache background refresh failed'. The same /api/scheduler/status reported server_load loop_lag latest_ms 0.0, heavy in_flight 0 and memory_guard engaged:false, so the server was demonstrably not busy. Shots: /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P-recheck/shots/Prc-home-0-en.png (no note at age 60), Prc-home-idle-age-note-en.png, Prc-home-idle-age-note-en-reload.png, Prc-home-idle-age-note-fr.png. Data: rc_main.json (stats0, stats_samples, home_strip_*), stats_idle_samples.txt. This is not by-design. Brief S3.4(d) (docs/design/AUTONOMOUS_SESSION_BRIEF_2026-09-02_CRASH_ROOT_CAUSE.md:825) asks for the note on a STALE-served payload. served_cache.py:233-240 itself says an idle, probe-verified entry 'is not merely fresh enough -- it is still exactly right'. Audit 11 (:473) praised the note as appearing 'only when the stats cache is genuinely stale', which this contradicts.
items.root_cause: src/static/app-home.js:117-137. homeStatsAgeNote decides on cache_age_s >= 90 alone and always appends '(server busy)'. src/api/served_cache.py:236-245 re-stamps checked_at but deliberately keeps built_at on an idle, probe-verified serve. _decorate (served_cache.py:139-153) exposes only as_of, cache_age_s and cached, never whether the value was verified unchanged or is waiting on a recount. So on every idle install the note fires 90 s after the first build and stays.
items.suggested_fix: In served_cache.cached, add a field to the decorated payload: `verified_current: probe is not None and probe == snapshot['probe']`, or `refresh_pending: True` when _kick_background_refresh ran. In homeStatsAgeNote, show the note only when the payload is not verified current, and word it by what is known ('as of {time} · recount pending') rather than asserting 'server busy'. Alternatively, add '(server busy)' only when /api/scheduler/status server_load shows heavy.in_flight > 0 or loop lag. Add a node test: an idle payload with age 400 and verified_current:true renders no note.

items.root_cause: src/api/search_omni.py:352-359 appends watched-page title_items after content_items without deduplicating by (wiki, title), so a watched page whose text was synced as a corpus article (article 448 ↔ WikiPage 1) is returned twice. src/static/app-shell.js:703-708 gives both rows the same label (it.title) and sub (it.wiki). The page_id row runs showTab('wiki'), which app-shell.js:117-121 redirects to Settings → Wikipedia. The code comment there still calls that 'the Wikipedia settings/tracker', but the tracker became Living sources' Wikipedia panel (openWikiTC, src/static/app-map.js:2951).
items.suggested_fix: Server: skip a title_item whose (wiki, title) matches a content_item already in the list. Or keep both and make each row say what it opens: the content row with sub '{wiki} · local copy' opening the reader, and the page row with sub '{wiki} · tracked changes' running openWikiTC(it.page_id, it.title, it.wiki). recheck.summary:
I reproduced all six of the walker's items on my own instance, and all six are confirmed on build 0deff9c4. The instance was a fresh encrypted seed (ui_clickthrough_seed plus the living-sources seed), booted locked on port 8971, unlocked through #pw, and kept in airplane mode throughout. Every consent popup was cancelled, with 0 off-host requests, 0 page or console errors and 0 HTTP >= 400.

- **P11 and the new Arabic wizard defect (same cause):** in ar, the wizard's #wiki-wizard-hosts line draws the '*.' of '*.wikipedia.org' at the far right end of the line (x=1034, while 'wikipedia' starts at x=487). The cause is app-sources.js:1388, which joins the hosts with no LTR isolation. The H3 isolate fix went only into the consent bubble (app-core.js:1329), and that bubble is correct in ar.
- **N375 and the new French Home overflow (same cause):** in fr at 375 px, Home scrolls sideways by 28 px, both after a live switch and after a reload. The strip items are white-space:nowrap (app.css:1440), so #home-stats grows to 366 px against a 301 px column. en, zh and ar measure 0, and so does every other N375 surface I measured in en, fr and ar: Settings → Wikipedia, the wizard, Living sources and the consent popup.
- **'(server busy)' on an idle app:** after 90 s idle, the strip says 'as of 10:11 AM (server busy)'. The server's cache had kept built_at 10:11:59 for 195 s against a 30 s TTL, which it does only when its write probe shows nothing was written, and server_load showed no lag and 0 heavy reads in flight. So the claim is false. The cause is homeStatsAgeNote (app-home.js:117-137), which keys on age alone because served_cache does not say whether a value is verified current. This is not by-design: brief S3.4(d) asks for the note only on a stale-served payload.
- **Palette's duplicate Wikipedia rows:** the Wikipedia group lists 'Coastal Infrastructure Act · en' twice. The first row opens the local reader (/api/articles/448/view). The second goes to #settings → Wikipedia, not to the page's tracked changes in Living sources. The cause is search_omni.py:352-359, which returns the same page twice without deduplicating, and app-shell.js:703-708, which gives both rows the same label and sub.

My server (PID 1557) is stopped by PID. Scripts, JSON and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/rewalk/P-recheck/.
